body:
Currently the "Hash Functions for Password Storage" subsection of the Cryptography appendix lists:

| Hash function | Reference | Required Parameter Sets | Status |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --|
| argon2 | RFC 9106 | Argon2ID: Memory Cost 19MB, Time Cost 2, Parallelism 1 | A |
| scrypt | RFC 7914 | 2^15 r = 8 p = 1 | A |
| bcrypt |[A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519476_A_Future-Adaptable_Password_Scheme) | At least 10 rounds. | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 210,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 600,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-1 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 1,300,000 iterations | L |

* For argon2, I would explicitly list argon2id in the fist column and, possibly include the other two variants Argon2d, Argon2i, Argon2id) to make it clearer if all are approved and if the same parameters should be used.
* For argon2 and sccrypt, maybe clarify that the parameters should be at least the ones given?
* For scrypt, it is not clear how "2^15" should be interpreted. Can we drop it?

So something like:

| Hash function | Reference | Required Parameter Sets | Status |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --|
| argon2id | RFC 9106 | Memory Cost ≥ 19MB, Time Cost ≥ 2, Parallelism = 1 | A |
| scrypt | RFC 7914 | r ≥ 8, p ≥ 1 | A |
| bcrypt |[A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519476_A_Future-Adaptable_Password_Scheme) | At least 10 rounds. | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 210,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 600,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-1 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 1,300,000 iterations | L |

comments.body:
> For argon2, I would explicitly list argon2id in the fist column and, possibly include the other two variants Argon2d, Argon2i, Argon2id) to make it clearer if all are approved and if the same parameters should be used.

Agree! I would drop Argon 2 and replace it with Argon2id. and only 2id. Argon2 and the other variants have side channel vulnerabilities.

> For argon2 and sccrypt, maybe clarify that the parameters should be at least the ones given?

Also agree.

> For scrypt, it is not clear how "2^15" should be interpreted. Can we drop it?

scrypt is kind of legacy, maybe even drop it?

Can we also change the table title from "hash function" to "Password Hash Function/KDF" ?

How about:

| Password Hash Function/KDF | Reference | Required Parameter Sets | Status |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --|
| argon2id | RFC 9106 | Memory Cost ≥ 19MB, Time Cost ≥ 2, Parallelism = 1 | A |
| scrypt | RFC 7914 | r ≥ 8, p ≥ 1 | A |
| bcrypt |[A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519476_A_Future-Adaptable_Password_Scheme) | At least 10 rounds. | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 210,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 600,000 iterations | A |
| PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-1 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | 1,300,000 iterations | L |

Hey @Sc00bz can you take a look at this please?
Can we also possibly drop the status column and drop legacy suggestions?

The issue with memory hard algorithms is memory and time parameters are inversely related for minimum settings. I guess you could pick one of the rows, but that would leave out some info. Maybe something like: Password Hash
Function/KDF | Reference | Required Parameter Sets -- | -- | -- Argon2id | RFC 9106 | m ≥ 47104 (46 MiB), t = 1, p = 1
m ≥ 19456 (19 MiB), t = 2, p = 1
m ≥ 12288 (12 MiB), t ≥ 3, p = 1 scrypt | RFC 7914 | N ≥ 2^17 (128 MiB), r = 8, p = 1
N ≥ 2^16 (64 MiB), r = 8, p = 2
N ≥ 2^15 (32 MiB), r = 8, p ≥ 3 bcrypt | [A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519476_A_Future-Adaptable_Password_Scheme) | cost ≥ 10 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | iterations ≥ 210,000 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | iterations ≥ 600,000 Or maybe: Password Hash
Function/KDF | Reference | Required Parameter Sets -- | -- | -- Argon2id | RFC 9106 | t = 1: m ≥ 47104 (46 MiB), p = 1
t = 2: m ≥ 19456 (19 MiB), p = 1
t ≥ 3: m ≥ 12288 (12 MiB), p = 1 scrypt | RFC 7914 | p = 1: N ≥ 2^17 (128 MiB), r = 8
p = 2: N ≥ 2^16 (64 MiB), r = 8
p ≥ 3: N ≥ 2^15 (32 MiB), r = 8 bcrypt | [A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519476_A_Future-Adaptable_Password_Scheme) | cost ≥ 10 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | iterations ≥ 210,000 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 | [NIST SP 800-132](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/132/final), [FIPS 180-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) | iterations ≥ 600,000
ps: @Sc00bz is one of the authors of the [password storage cheatsheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) and I give his edits here two big thumbs up.

> Can we also possibly drop the status column and drop legacy suggestions?

I'd keep the status column because it is all over the place in the appendix :)

Can we say that PBKDF2 is legacy (because it is not memory hard)?

We had PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-1 included as legacy because AFAIU it is not completely broken. (→ if you are currently using it, you should consider a migration plan but you don't have to panic just yet ?) Shall we keep it?

PBKDF2 is the only NIST approved password KDF. They do mention Balloon Hashing but there is no specification for it. Some have tried to claim scrypt is NIST approved because its output is PBKDF2, but this is only to trick auditors into giving it a pass. The non-constant runtime based on secrets would bar it from being NIST approved.
+1 @Sc00bz I would not consider PBKDF2 to be legacy.
See #3021. How should we handle the duplication between the list of "Hash Functions for Password Storage" and the list of "(Password-based) KDFs"?

> PBKDF2 is the only NIST approved password KDF. They do mention Balloon Hashing but there is no specification for it. Some have tried to claim scrypt is NIST approved because its output is PBKDF2, but this is only to trick auditors into giving it a pass. The non-constant runtime based on secrets would bar it from being NIST approved.

Agree with this. Would only add that this 'scrypt trick' isn't reliable, and for cryptography NIST is very strongly the baseline for many orgs, especially CNI and those who are their providers.

I agree with removing scrypt.

But Argon2id is the most secure choice and is commonly used.

PBKDF2 is a weaker choice but is a NIST standard.

I would even drop bcrypt these days since it has a size limit.
